name: Pashmina Shawl
description: Hand-spun fine wool shawl woven from Changthangi goat hair, prized for centuries for its warmth and softness.

name: Kashmiri Papier-Mache
description: Intricately hand-painted decorative objects made from paper pulp, a Persian-origin craft flourishing in Kashmir since the 14th century.

name: Chikankari Embroidery
description: Delicate white-thread hand embroidery on fine fabric, originating in Mughal-era Lucknow.

name: Banarasi Silk Saree
description: Opulent silk sarees woven with gold and silver brocade, a Varanasi weaving tradition over 500 years old.

name: Moradabad Brassware
description: Ornate hand-engraved brass utensils and decor, earning Moradabad the title 'Brass City of India'.

name: Madhubani Painting
description: Vivid folk paintings using natural dyes, traditionally created by women of the Mithila region on walls and now on paper/canvas.

name: Kanchipuram Silk Saree
description: Heavy silk sarees with wide contrast borders and temple-inspired motifs, woven by artisan families for generations.

name: Thanjavur Painting
description: Classical South Indian painting style using gold foil, semi-precious stones, and rich colors, dating to the Maratha court era.

name: Channapatna Toys
description: Colorful lacquered wooden toys and dolls, a craft tradition dating back to Tipu Sultan's era.

name: Bidriware
description: Distinctive blackened metal handicraft inlaid with silver, originating in 14th-century Bidar under Bahmani rule.

name: Mysore Silk Saree
description: Pure silk sarees with a signature sheen, woven using silk from KSIC's own mills since the 1930s.

name: Pochampally Ikat
description: Geometric tie-dye woven textiles, earning Pochampally village the nickname 'Silk City of India'.

name: Kondapalli Toys
description: Lightweight wooden toys carved from local Tella Poniki wood, depicting rural life and mythology.

name: Bastar Dhokra Art
description: Ancient lost-wax metal casting technique used by tribal artisans to create bronze figurines and decor.

name: Pattachitra Painting
description: Cloth-based scroll paintings with mythological themes, made using natural pigments by traditional Chitrakar artist families.

name: Sambalpuri Saree
description: Handwoven sarees using the distinctive Bandha (tie-dye) technique, featuring traditional Odia motifs like shankha and chakra.

name: Bankura Terracotta
description: Iconic elongated-neck terracotta horses and folk art, hand-shaped by traditional Kumbhakar potter communities.

name: Kutch Embroidery
description: Vibrant mirror-work embroidery practiced by multiple pastoral communities of the Kutch desert region, each with a distinct style.

name: Patan Patola
description: Double ikat silk sarees so intricate that a single piece can take up to a year to weave, historically worn by royalty.

name: Blue Pottery
description: Persian-influenced glazed pottery made without clay, using quartz powder, distinctive for its cobalt blue dye.

name: Bagru Hand Block Print
description: Natural dye hand-block textile printing tradition practiced by the Chhipa community in Bagru village for over 300 years.

name: Phulkari Embroidery
description: Vibrant floral thread-work embroidery on shawls and dupattas, traditionally made by women for weddings and festivals.

name: Warli Painting
description: Minimalist tribal wall art using geometric white shapes on mud backgrounds, practiced by the Warli tribe for centuries.

name: Aranmula Kannadi
description: Handcrafted metal mirrors made from a secret bronze alloy, produced by only a few families in Aranmula village.

name: Nagaland Bamboo Craft
description: Traditional bamboo and cane products including baskets, mats, and furniture, integral to Naga tribal daily life and festivals.

name: Kani Shawl
description: Intricately woven shawls using small wooden 'kani' sticks instead of a shuttle, taking months to complete one piece.

name: Walnut Wood Carving
description: Ornately carved furniture and decor made from Kashmir walnut wood, renowned for its fine grain and durability.

name: Banaras Brocade
description: Rich zari-woven brocade fabric used in sarees and garments, a Varanasi weaving specialty distinct from plain silk.

name: Lucknow Zardozi
description: Heavy metallic thread embroidery using gold and silver wire, historically adorning royal garments.

name: Firozabad Glassware
description: Hand-blown coloured glass bangles and decorative items, earning Firozabad the title 'Glass City of India'.

name: Meerut Scissors
description: Traditional hand-forged scissors and cutting tools, a centuries-old metalworking craft of Meerut.

name: Sanganeri Hand Block Print
description: Fine hand block printing tradition distinct from Bagru, known for delicate floral motifs on light backgrounds.

name: Kota Doria
description: Lightweight, sheer cotton-silk fabric woven in a distinctive checkered pattern called khat.

name: Molela Clay Work
description: Terracotta plaques depicting deities and folk gods, handmade by the Kumhar potter community of Molela village.

name: Meenakari Jewelry
description: Vivid enamel work on gold and silver jewelry, a Mughal-era craft perfected by Jaipur's artisans.

name: Pipli Applique Work
description: Colourful applique craft using cutout fabric patches, traditionally used for temple umbrellas and canopies.

name: Konark Stone Carving
description: Intricate stone sculpture tradition famous for the carvings of the Konark Sun Temple.

name: Cuttack Silver Filigree
description: Delicate silver wire jewelry and decor, hand-twisted into intricate lace-like patterns by Cuttack's silversmiths.

name: Baluchari Saree
description: Silk sarees woven with elaborate mythological and courtly scenes on the pallu, originating in the Murshidabad region.

name: Dhaniakhali Saree
description: Fine cotton sarees with a distinctive red border, woven in the Dhaniakhali region of Hooghly district.

name: Nakshi Kantha
description: Hand-embroidered quilts and textiles using running stitch to create intricate folk motifs, a Bengal tradition passed through generations.

name: Purulia Chau Mask
description: Vividly painted papier-mache masks worn during the traditional Chau dance-drama of Purulia.

name: Santiniketan Leather Goods
description: Hand-tooled and batik-dyed leather bags and accessories originating from the Santiniketan region founded by Tagore.

name: Muga Silk
description: The world's only golden-hued silk, produced from silkworms native to Assam, prized for its natural sheen and durability.

name: Sarthebari Bell Metal Craft
description: Traditional bell metal utensils and ritual items hand-hammered by artisans of Sarthebari village.

name: Naga Shawl Weaving
description: Distinctively patterned tribal shawls woven by Naga communities, with designs signifying clan and social status.

name: Moirang Phee
description: Handwoven textile with distinctive temple-border motifs, traditionally worn by Manipuri women.

name: Toda Embroidery
description: Distinctive red-and-black embroidery on white cotton shawls, practiced by the Toda tribal community of the Nilgiris.

name: Mahabalipuram Stone Sculpture
description: Granite stone sculpture tradition dating to the Pallava dynasty, famous for the rock-cut monuments of Mahabalipuram.

name: Thanjavur Bommai
description: Traditional bobble-head dolls hand-painted in vivid colours, a folk craft distinct from Thanjavur paintings.

name: Bhavani Jamakkalam
description: Thick handwoven cotton floor rugs with characteristic mixed-colour warp threads, woven in Bhavani town.

name: Salem Silk
description: Pure mulberry silk textiles woven in Salem, known for their fine texture and vibrant natural dyes.

name: Kolhapuri Chappal
description: Handcrafted leather sandals made using vegetable-tanned leather, worn for centuries and famous worldwide.

name: Paithani Saree
description: Richly woven silk sarees with peacock and floral motifs and a distinctive oblique square border.

name: Himroo Shawl
description: Woven fabric blending cotton, silk, and zari, historically developed as an affordable alternative to Kinkhwab brocade.

name: Bhagalpuri Tussar Silk
description: Wild tussar silk textiles, earning Bhagalpur the nickname 'Silk City of Bihar'.

name: Sujini Embroidery
description: Hand-stitched quilted embroidery depicting rural life and folklore, traditionally made by women of Bihar.

name: Sikki Grass Craft
description: Fine golden grass woven into decorative boxes, toys and idols, a traditional Mithila handicraft.

name: Chanderi Saree
description: Sheer, lightweight sarees woven with gold and silver zari, blending silk and cotton threads.

name: Maheshwari Saree
description: Distinctive reversible-border sarees woven in Maheshwar, patronised by Holkar queen Ahilyabai.

name: Gond Painting
description: Vivid dot-and-line folk art created by the Gond tribal community depicting nature and mythology.

name: Bastar Wood Carving
description: Intricately carved wooden sculptures and masks made by tribal artisans of Bastar, depicting deities and folklore.

name: Kashmiri Hand-Knotted Carpet
description: Hand-knotted silk and wool carpets with intricate Persian-influenced patterns, woven knot-by-knot on traditional looms.

name: Sujani Craft of Bihar
description: Layered cotton quilts hand-stitched with running stitch to depict social and rural themes, a Bihar craft tradition.

name: Dokra Metal Craft of Bengal
description: Ancient lost-wax metal casting technique producing bronze figurines, practiced by tribal artisans of West Bengal.
